title: Tower of London
summary: Historic castle on the north bank of the River Thames in London, founded toward the end of 1066 during the Norman Conquest. Its White Tower was a symbol of Norman power. Over time it served as royal residence, prison, armoury, treasury and home of the Crown Jewels, and it is now a World Heritage Site.

as_recorded.value: It was founded toward the end of 1066 as part of the Norman Conquest.
William the Conqueror built the White Tower in 1066

importance.justification: Iconic Norman fortress and royal palace central to English state, monarchy and prison history; UNESCO World Heritage Site.

audience_note: Mentions imprisonment, torture reputation and executions, including of queens.

sources.title: Tower of London - UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: Sources differ on dating: Wikipedia says founded toward end of 1066 and the White Tower built in 1078; UNESCO says the White Tower was built in 1066. Used 1066 as the founding year. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Wikipedia, UNESCO; quotes machine-checked.)
